title: Effect of hydrocortisone on mortality in patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP Corticosteroid Domain Randomized Clinical Trial
shortTitle: REMAP-CAP: fixed-course hydrocortisone did not show a large mortality benefit
summary: This adaptive platform comparison assigned 658 ICU patients with severe CAP to hydrocortisone 50 mg IV every 6 hours for 7 days or no corticosteroid. Enrollment stopped for futility. Ninety-day mortality was 15.0% versus 9.8%; stratum-specific adjusted ORs were 1.52–1.63, with all 95% credible intervals crossing 1.
whyItMatters: Complicates the assumption that every severe-CAP steroid regimen produces the same benefit. This tested regimen does not by itself invalidate other regimens or current guideline-directed care.
limitations: The control arm was small (122 patients), 15 outcomes were missing, and Bayesian estimates were imprecise. Smaller benefits and harm remain possible; adverse-event detail was not verified beyond the abstract.
population: Adults admitted to ICU with severe community-acquired pneumonia.
intervention: Fixed 7-day IV hydrocortisone, 50 mg every 6 hours.
primaryEndpoint: All-cause mortality at 90 days, stratified by influenza and shock.
findings: Stopping criterion: <5% probability of a >20% relative mortality improvement.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. Primary abstract reviewed; full article not reviewed. Publisher correction of June 16, 2025 reviewed: corresponding author was erroneously listed as an additional author; no result correction stated.
